title: Polymer clay gradient ocean wave clip
subtitle: A hair clip decorated with blended blue and white polymer clay in a wave pattern
excerpt: A plain alligator clip or barrette base is fitted with a polymer clay tile in a blue-to-white gradient pattern suggesting an ocean wave. The gradient is made by blending the two colours in stages across the tile width. No kiln is required: the clay hardens at 130°C in a domestic oven.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that hardens in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C

content.text: A wave-gradient tile is one of the most accessible projects for
beginners. Blending two colours in incremental steps gives the gradient. The tile is glued to a plain clip base after curing. No kiln is required.

materials.name: Plain alligator clip or barrette base

content.text: Condition the blue and white separately. Roll each into a log about 5 cm long.

Pinch a small piece from one end of the blue log and a slightly larger piece from the adjacent end of the white log. Blend those two pieces together by rolling into a new log; this gives a pale blue. Repeat with progressively more white added to get five tones from deep blue to pure white.

Roll each tone into a thin slab roughly 2 mm thick and 1 cm wide. Lay the five slabs side by side in order of tone from dark to light, then roll over all of them lightly to join the edges into one blended slab.
Cut a rectangle from the blended slab to fit the clip base, trimming with a fettling knife to 3 mm thick and the length and width of the clip face.
Use a bamboo skewer or fingernail to press gentle undulating curves into the surface, following the horizontal gradient direction to suggest waves on water. Keep the lines shallow.

Place the tile on a ceramic tile and cure at 130°C for 20 minutes. Ventilate the kitchen. Cool fully. Glue to the clip base with cyanoacrylate adhesive. Hold for 60 seconds and leave to set for 24 hours before wearing.
Use terracotta-to-peach or emerald-to-sage green for a different palette. Cut the tile into an oval rather than a rectangle for a smoother look.

items.problem: Gradient shows hard lines between tones rather than smooth blending
items.cause: Adjacent tone slabs were not joined by rolling before cutting the tile
items.fix: Roll the slab assembly more firmly with the rolling pin across the tone boundaries to encourage the edge colours to merge slightly. A light smoothing pass with a wet fingertip after rolling also softens visible joins

items.problem: Tile lifts or pops off the clip after a few days
items.cause: Adhesive did not bond well to the smooth cured clay surface
items.fix: Scuff the tile back with 120-grit sandpaper, apply fresh adhesive, and clamp overnight to bond.
